analysis.investment_thesis: At 42x earnings and 8.64x book value, Elgi Equipments is priced entirely on the story of future global compressor market share — precisely the kind of speculative valuation I have warned against for seventy years. The business has genuine merits, but I will not pay three times my maximum P/E for them.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 10.7% with net profit CAGR of 23.9% over nine years reflects a genuine compounding business with international scale
D/E of 0.26 is manageable and OCF has been positive in 5 of the last 5 years with FCF growing to INR 298 Cr in FY25
Strong institutional endorsement with FII holding of 22.2% — while this bids up the price, it reflects genuine recognition of product quality
key_risks: P/E of 42x is nearly three times my maximum threshold of 15x — the stock is priced to perfection with zero tolerance for any earnings disappointment
P/B of 8.64x means tangible assets back only 12 rupees of every 100 rupees invested; a business setback would reveal almost no asset-based floor to the price
Operating margin of 12.22% is modest for a premium-priced industrial company — minor input cost increases or competitive pressure could compress earnings rapidly
red_flags: P/E of 42x — the most extreme valuation in this peer group and wildly inconsistent with my definition of a margin of safety
P/B of 8.64x — paying 8.6 times net asset value for a manufacturer of physical compressors is a purely speculative wager on brand and growth
OCF was only INR 35 Cr in FY20 on INR 1,829 Cr of revenue — a 1.9% cash conversion rate — demonstrating how quickly this business can consume rather than generate cash
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Elgi Equipments is a quality manufacturer with a coherent international ambition and a satisfying multi-decade operating history. I do not question the products or management intent. But quality and price are entirely separate questions, and at 42x trailing earnings, the price answers only one question: how much optimism can be packed into a share? The EV/EBITDA of 32x exceeds every reasonable metric I have ever endorsed for an established industrial manufacturer.

My 'margin of safety' principle exists precisely for situations like this: when a business is good but the price is extraordinary, the investor bears all the risk with none of the reward. Elgi's OCF of only INR 35 Cr on INR 1,829 Cr of revenue in FY20 — a 1.9% OCF margin — is a powerful reminder of how cyclically sensitive this business remains under stress. At today's price of INR 549, the investor who buys is speculating, not investing. The Graham Number for this stock, even generously calculated, is likely below INR 200. I would require a price decline of 50–60% before any reconsideration.
